It is `varint` :wink: It's a variable-length integer ( https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/encoding#varints )

Oh yeah, do not focus too much on it. It is a stripped down version of [pbf](https://github.com/mapbox/pbf) (a protobuf implementation) with only the methods that are useful to us to keep it as light as possible (since the original implementation is not tree-shakable).
Agree, but for now in this POC I just made it "works" :wink:, then is still tons of improvement in quality/structure/testing to do.

This file (`schema.proto`) is only needed to generate the JavaScript counterpart (`schema.js`), I put it there for simplicity but it should live it's own project imho (since it is meant to be shared between the client and the server).

For `schema.js`, it is needed in the client so we can use it to generate the message and map all `$$type` and `$$params` to a number to keep the message as light as possible.
Yes that's also a possibility, I will update the implementation to do this.

This part is very hacky here:

* It should be in headers, not in queryParameters
* `instantSearchInstance.client.transporter.queryParameters` is typed at read-only, so to do it properly we'll need to have a proper method to update it

I was not planning to be compatible with the client v3 (since we'll need to do some update to the client to properly set the header). Do you thing this is something we should do?

unknown request parameters of the client will go to either headers or query parameters (v4):

```
search([], { someParameter: "value", headers: { someHeader: "value })
```

v3 doesn't have any options for that, but at least it should ignore the second parameter
